checkpoints: After `retire()` returns during `open(id)`, verify that the opening request is still current before creating or publishing the new view.
After callback-capable `setView(...)`, store subscription callbacks, rendering callbacks, and delayed save callbacks, do not let an obsolete request publish stale document/view state.
When a 120 ms save callback fires, clear its trailing-task ticket/value so a later editing burst can schedule and save normally.
On `close()` or `dispose()`, remove the live badge subscription and render no current document while retaining document-buffer ownership in `BufferBank`.
Verify public JavaScript/JSX syntax/build checks after any Action; those checks do not establish business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not write the workspace draft to the store on every `edit(text)` call.
Do not publish intermediate texts from the same editing burst.
Do not change the search preview or its separate 40 ms quiet interval.
Do not make the current view badge own or destroy document buffers.
Do not change the public methods `open(id)`, `edit(text)`, `close()`, `dispose()`, `query(text)`, or `hide()`.
Do not allow synchronous callback reentry from an obsolete `open` request to overwrite or render over the newer navigation result.
Do not alter source identities, text values, status payload semantics, or the synchronous store API.
lifecycle_identity: A document buffer is identified by document `id` and is owned by the coordinator's separate `BufferBank`, not by the currently displayed view badge.
Repeated access to the same document `id` within one coordinator returns the same trailing buffer, allowing subsequent editing bursts to continue saving.
The live view consists of the currently opened document identity plus its badge subscription; navigation retires that view without transferring buffer ownership to it.
The search preview owns a distinct trailing task and lifecycle from workspace document buffers.

obligations.text: Each workspace `edit(text)` for a live view must enqueue that view's document buffer through the existing trailing-task utility instead of writing immediately to the store.
For edits in one burst, reset the document buffer's delay on every edit and, after 120 ms with no newer edit, write exactly the latest text from that burst to the store.
After a burst saves, the same document buffer must remain capable of scheduling and saving later bursts.
Workspace document buffers must remain separate from the current view badge and keyed by document identity through `BufferBank`.
Opening, closing, disposing, document rendering, and status subscription behavior must otherwise retain their existing public interfaces and observable semantics.
Synchronous navigation triggered by callback-capable boundaries must win over an older in-progress `open`; the older request must not subsequently install or render stale view state.
The adjacent search preview must remain unchanged, including its independent 40 ms trailing task and `query`/`hide` interface.

ordering_barriers: Within a document editing burst: accept edit text, cancel any prior scheduled ticket, remember the newest text, schedule one 120 ms flush, then write that newest text when the quiet interval expires.
A delayed document save writes through `env.store.write(id,text)`; because store delivery is synchronous, all resulting subscription/navigation callbacks occur before that write returns.
During navigation, invalidate the previous request and retire the old live view before installing the replacement view.

Treat `setView`, `env.renderDocument`, `env.renderStatus`, `env.store.write`, and subscription delivery as callback-capable boundaries; after reentry, an older request may not continue publishing state unless its request identity is still current.

Install the current view identity/subscription before rendering its document, while ensuring any synchronous reentrant navigation caused during installation or rendering cannot be overwritten by the outer request.
preservation: Preserve the editor's `open`, `edit`, `close`, and `dispose` public interface.
Preserve synchronous store `read`, `write`, and `subscribe` behavior and existing event payload semantics.
Preserve opening a document with its current stored text and forwarding matching store events to status rendering.
Preserve navigation cleanup of the prior live subscription and rendering of no document on retirement.
Preserve document buffers independently of the current view badge.
Preserve the search preview's transient ownership and different quiet interval.
Preserve all original source identities/text and status payload meanings.
scope: Change only workspace draft-edit coordination needed to route edits through the existing per-document trailing buffer.
The relevant business code is `src/coordinator.js`, with `src/services.js` supplying the existing trailing-task behavior and `src/Workspace.jsx` supplying the public React host lifecycle.
Search preview behavior in `src/services.js` is explicitly outside the maintenance change.

Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

Editorial coordination — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: separate BufferBank service

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };

const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};
useImperativeHandle(ref,()=>api,[api]);useEffect(()=>api.dispose,[api]);
These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations.

triggers: A caller invokes workspace `edit(text)` while a document view is live.

A caller invokes search preview `query(text)` or `hide()`; this remains governed by its existing independent behavior.
unknowns: The public sources do not specify whether pending document edits must flush, remain scheduled, or be canceled on `close()`, `dispose()`, or navigation; existing `BufferBank` independence suggests they are not automatically owned by view retirement, but the exact policy is not stated explicitly.
The public sources do not define exception-handling semantics if timer, store, subscription, view-setting, or rendering callbacks throw.
The public sources do not state whether opening the same document again should immediately reflect a pending unsaved buffer value or only the current synchronous store value.
The public sources do not define behavior for invalid document identifiers or non-string edit values; retain existing pass-through semantics.

The exact set of callbacks that may synchronously navigate is not exhaustively enumerated, although save/store listeners are explicitly identified and current source callbacks are observable reentry boundaries.
